_comment: Tier-2 for skfem adaptive_poisson#1, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: MeshTri.refined takes ELEMENT indices, a boolean mask of length n_elements works, and passing facet indices raises IndexError 'index N is out of bounds for axis 0 with size M'. Ran: MeshTri().refined(2) (32 elements, 56 facets, 25 vertices); the same three elements marked by index and by mask; the full facet index array; an out-of-range index; and a scalar argument. Printed: index and mask give identical meshes -- 47 elements each, identical connectivity and points. Facet indices raise IndexError 'index 32 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 32' -- note AXIS 1, not the axis 0 the entry quotes, and the size in the message is the ELEMENT count (32), not the facet count (56), so a gate matching the literal 'axis 0' or looking for the facet count would miss it. NEW AND SILENT: a SCALAR argument is not 'refine that element' -- refined(3) is the uniform-refinement overload and multiplies 32 elements to 2048 with no warning, while refined(np.array([3])) gives 39. That is the shape a mask/index mix-up most easily takes.
